body: Primal is Sony's PlayStation 2 action-adventure, first released in North America on 25 March 2003. Jen travels through supernatural realms with Scree, a gargoyle companion, trying to restore a balance that has been disturbed. Her ability to take demonic forms changes how these places can be explored. The adventure combines combat with puzzles and a continuing relationship between its two leads. Instead of treating a new world as only another set of enemies, the game makes it a place whose rules Jen must learn before she can reach everything within it.

Each realm introduces a transformation with capabilities suited to its environment. An underwater area becomes accessible through the Undine form, while other abilities change the use of time or movement. Later obstacles ask the player to combine what has already been learned, giving a return to a familiar place another purpose. Scree provides a second character within that exploration. The player switches attention between their strengths, reading a problem in terms of who can act and which form gives Jen the means to continue through it.

The Cambridge team gave considerable attention to the setting, characters and voice performances, with music by Paul Arnold, Andrew Barnabas and the band 16Volt. Reviews praised those aspects while finding the combat, puzzles and controls less consistent. Sony had hoped to establish a new major series, but sales fell short and an early sequel plan was shelved. The European release arrived in April 2003. Primal remains associated with its central partnership and atmosphere, showing how a console adventure could build its identity around two characters learning to depend on one another.
